newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire's new army chief discreet on strategy.
newsitem.headline: Zaire's new army chief discreet on strategy.

text.p: Zaire's new army chief pledged on Thursday to recover territory lost to Rwandan-backed rebels but gave no details of how he would go about it.

"Given the sensitivity of the job, I ask you to understand if I do not give you many details. I am a military man and do not meddle in politics," General Mahele Bokungo told reporters after meeting President Mobutu Sese Seko.
"I assure you that with the help of God, and the support of all the Zairean people, we will fulfil this mission," he added.

Mobutu returned home on Tuesday after four months of cancer treatment in Europe. A day after his arrival he entrusted Mahele with the job of bringing order to Zaire's ragged army and fighting Rwandan-backed rebels who have seized large swathes of territory in the east.

Mahele, an experienced and respected officer trained in France and Israel, and by Zaire's former Belgian colonial rulers, has been granted unprecedented powers to control the hitherto untouchable presidential guard.

Rebel leader Laurent Kabila urged civilians on Thursday to stay, but his words failed to stem a stream of people leaving the eastern city of Goma, the biggest of several towns seized by rebels since fighting erupted in October.
In a speech on rebel Star Radio, Kabila said his forces would defeat any army counter-attack launched by Mobutu.
Zaire's political opposition reacted cautiously to an invitation by Mobutu to join a crisis government he wants formed by the weekend.
"The president was clear. A crisis government must be in place by midday Saturday, a government run by a credible man who has the support of the people," he told Reuters.
Marcel Mbayo, an adviser to radical opposition leader Etienne Tshisekedi, said there was no constitutional basis for Mobutu's planned changes.
"We are waiting for the heads of the two political families (Mobutu and Tshisekedi) to meet before we can decide what we are going to do," Mbayo told Reuters.
